title: Two to five targeted missed-injury records changed annual ozone by moisture signs in four eastern US forest samples in 1994-2010
abstract: We tested how missed visible plant injury can change a joint ozone and soil moisture estimate. Four US Northeast and North Central samples in 1994-2002 and 2003-2010 used 5,277 site-year records from a verified published panel. Fixed models separated annual exposure products from site means and controlled for weather, sampling effort, site and year. Exact coefficient weights showed that two to five selected zero-to-one changes crossed zero in each sample, or 0.11 to 0.70 percent of records. The limits stayed the same with at most one change per site. One fewer optimal change kept the original sign. No sign changed in 10,000 uniform random trials per sample at those budgets. Thus the result concerns targeted errors, not an estimated error rate. Prior sampling intervals already included zero. Unknown false negatives, fixed design assumptions, coarse exposure and repeated source records limit inference. We provide a proof, original code, aggregate bounds, direct numerical checks, source hashes and external data retrieval instructions. The result does not show that a specific record is wrong or that ozone harms biodiversity.

display.caption: Exact coefficient limits when at most a fixed number of recorded zeros can change to injury. These are fixed-design worst-case limits, not sampling intervals. Red points are observed annual-product coefficients. Targeted errors are not measured error rates.
